content.value_statement: Email tests often produce noisy winners because they lack power, guardrails, or clean controls. This skill creates structured test plans and read-outs with clear promotion decisions.
actual_capabilities: Selects an A/B, multivariate, send-time, or hold-out test mode from the user request.
Writes falsifiable hypotheses and variant matrices that isolate one variable per cell.
Estimates sample size, minimum detectable effect, duration, and power from baseline rates.
Defines primary, secondary, and guardrail metrics for email experiment goals.
Reads finished ESP exports and gives a promote, kill, or keep-testing decision.
limitations: Does not write the subject line, email body, preheader, or CTA being tested.
Does not compute program-wide SEND EQS or run deliverability veto gates.
Needs user-provided baselines, list size, send volume, or ESP results exports.
Documents statistical methods but does not run code or call live ESP APIs by default.

use_cases.title: Plan a Subject-Line Test
use_cases.description: Create a powered A/B plan with a control, open-rate target, duration, and no-peeking rule before launch.

use_cases.title: Compare Send Times
use_cases.description: Design a send-time test that holds creative and segment constant while comparing same-window engagement.

use_cases.title: Read Finished Results
use_cases.description: Review ESP export counts, name the significance method, and decide whether to promote, kill, or keep testing.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Basic A/B Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an A/B subject-line test for a retention email. Baseline open rate is 38%, list size is 12,000, and I want to detect a 3-point lift.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Send-Time Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a send-time test for my weekly newsletter. Baseline open rate is 40%, list size is 20,000, and I can send once per week.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Multivariate Matrix
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 2 by 2 subject and CTA multivariate test. Baseline click rate is 2.1%, list size is 80,000, and the minimum practical lift is 0.5 points.

prompt_templates.title: Read Out Completed Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze my completed email test export with delivered, opens, clicks, conversions, unsubscribes, and complaints by variant. Tell me whether to promote, kill, or keep testing.

output_examples.input: A retention subject-line test with 38% baseline open rate and 12,000 recipients.
output_examples.output: The skill returns an A/B plan with one subject change, a control, an estimated sample per cell, a fixed read date, and guardrails for unsubscribes and complaints.

output_examples.input: A newsletter team wants to test Tuesday morning against Thursday afternoon.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends a send-time design that randomizes the segment, keeps creative constant, compares same-window engagement, and covers a full weekday cycle.

output_examples.input: A finished ESP export shows higher clicks for variant B but more complaints.
output_examples.output: The skill applies the significance gate, checks the guardrail breach, and recommends killing the variant instead of promoting a risky winner.

best_practices: Change only one variable per cell so the result is attributable.
Set the sample size, minimum practical lift, and read date before launch.
Use unsubscribe, complaint, and hard-bounce guardrails before promoting a winner.
anti_patterns: Calling a winner before the planned sample size or read date.
Changing subject, CTA, and creative in the same test cell.
Promoting a statistically significant lift that misses the practical lift or violates guardrails.

faq.question: Can this skill write the email creative?
faq.answer: No. It designs the experiment and read-out. Use an email creative skill for subject lines, body copy, and CTAs.

faq.question: What data do I need for a new test?
faq.answer: Provide the test idea, baseline rate, list size or daily send volume, and the minimum lift worth detecting.

faq.question: What data do I need for a completed test?
faq.answer: Provide delivered counts and outcome counts by variant, plus unsubscribe, complaint, and bounce metrics when available.

faq.question: Does it support hold-out tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It can design randomized send versus no-send hold-outs and size them on conversion or revenue metrics.

faq.question: Does it run live API calls to an ESP?
faq.answer: No. It works from user-provided exports by default. Optional connectors are not required for the core workflow.

faq.question: How does it decide whether to promote a winner?
faq.answer: It requires statistical significance, the minimum practical lift, and intact guardrails before recommending promotion.
